rationale: Start with a broad mid-strength scouting gradient at moderate temperature to spread unknown compounds across the run and reveal overall retention, selectivity, and whether any compounds are missing. This gives a balanced first map before narrowing conditions in later injections.

All compounds eluted cleanly and fairly early, so reduce final strength to hold late compounds longer and redistribute the gradient over the crowded mid-region around 5.9–6.5 min. Keeping phi0, tG, and T fixed isolates the effect of gradient range on selectivity and spacing.

Resolution is already perfect, so the only way to improve CRF is to shorten analysis time while preserving full elution and acceptable spacing. A steeper version of the successful first gradient should test whether the last peak can be brought earlier without collapsing the crowded central cluster.

Injection 3 is nearly optimal but slightly over-compressed the critical 6/7 pair, so lengthening the successful gradient a little should recover full resolution while keeping the time term near zero. This is a local refinement around the current best condition.

The best score is already near 1.0, so now probe a small selectivity change rather than a larger timing change. Lowering temperature slightly may open the critical 6/7 pair under the faster 14 min gradient while keeping the run short enough to preserve the zero time penalty.

Lowering temperature worsened selectivity, so test the opposite direction with a small temperature increase while keeping the best fast gradient. If 45 C slightly improves the critical cluster without pushing the last peak much later, it could surpass the current best.

Temperature changes hurt the critical pair, so return to 40 C and make a small solvent-profile change instead. Lowering phi0 may expand the early-to-mid gradient region and subtly alter spacing in the crowded cluster while preserving the short run and strong final elution.

Probe phi0 in the opposite direction from injection 7 while keeping the best fast method framework. A slightly higher starting organic may reshuffle the crowded mid-eluting group and improve the critical 6/7 separation without adding a time penalty.

The best region is clearly around the 14 min, 40 C method, so make a small decrease in phi1 to slightly flatten the gradient and try to open the persistent 6/7 critical pair. This targets a modest selectivity gain while likely keeping the last peak early enough for no time penalty.

Now that the maximum score has been reached, the only worthwhile exploration is robustness around the optimum. Shortening tG slightly tests whether an even faster method can retain full resolution and the zero time penalty, or whether 14 minutes is the true local optimum.

Since phi1 = 0.85 at 14 minutes gave the optimum, test a small additional decrease in final organic to see whether the critical 6/7 pair opens further while still keeping the last peak within the zero-penalty region. This is a tight local refinement around the current optimum.

The optimum at 14 minutes may sit on a narrow ridge, so test a slightly longer gradient at the same phi1 = 0.85 to map robustness on the slow side. This checks whether full resolution is maintained with only a small time cost, helping confirm the shape of the local optimum.

The optimum is well defined in tG and T, so the most informative remaining local test is a small increase in phi0 at the optimal phi1 = 0.85. This may preserve the zero time penalty while slightly improving or at least stress-testing the selectivity of the persistent 6/7 critical pair.

A second 1.000 score at higher phi0 suggests a flat optimum ridge in that direction, so step phi0 up once more to map the boundary of the zero-penalty/full-resolution region. This may reveal an equally optimal but faster or more robust operating point.

Having mapped higher phi0, test the lower side at the same optimal phi1, tG, and T to bracket the flat optimum ridge. This should identify whether phi0 = 0.10–0.15 is truly best or if lower starting strength can also maintain full resolution with zero time penalty.

The best region appears centered near phi0 0.10–0.15 and phi1 0.85, so test a diagonal nearby point to map the local plateau rather than repeating known inferior edges. This checks whether the higher phi0 that gave 1.000 remains optimal when paired with a slightly lower phi1, potentially improving robustness of the critical cluster.

Both 1.000 methods use the same phi1 and tG but differ only slightly in phi0, so the remaining useful question is whether phi0 = 0.15 tolerates a shorter gradient better than phi0 = 0.10. This directly tests whether the alternate optimum has a steeper speed–resolution tradeoff and could define the practical edge of the optimum plateau.

Since the composition space around phi0/phi1/tG is now well mapped, a final useful robustness probe is temperature at the optimal solvent program. This tests whether the 1.000 method is temperature-sensitive or whether a nearby higher-temperature operating point could remain on the optimum plateau.

Higher temperature clearly harms the critical pair, so test the lower-temperature side at the alternate 1.000 solvent program to complete the robustness map around the optimum. This checks whether phi0 = 0.15 is any less temperature-sensitive than phi0 = 0.10 while staying in the proven best gradient region.

With six injections left and the maximum already achieved, the remaining value is mapping the nearby high-phi0/high-compression corner to define the edge of the optimum plateau. This combination extends the local grid systematically and tests whether both phi0 increase and phi1 decrease together remain acceptable or collapse the critical pair.

A third 1.000 point extending toward higher phi0 suggests the optimum plateau may continue in that direction, so step phi0 up once more at the successful phi1 = 0.80. This efficiently probes the edge of the plateau and may identify the fastest practical high-phi0 operating point before early peaks become too compressed.

The failure at phi0 = 0.25 shows the high-phi0 edge is driven by over-compression of the earliest peaks, so lower phi0 back to the last successful value and decrease phi1 one step to explore the adjacent plateau boundary in a safer direction. This tests whether the 1.000 region extends toward lower final strength without recreating the early coelution problem.

Phi0 = 0.20 and phi1 = 0.80 gave another 1.000 point, so the most informative remaining test is whether this higher-phi0 optimum tolerates a shorter gradient as well as the lower-phi0 optima. This maps the fast edge of that plateau branch and could reveal whether it is more or less robust than the 0.10/0.85 and 0.15/0.85 conditions.

The remaining unexplored neighbor of the successful phi0 = 0.20, tG = 14, T = 40 region is higher phi1, which will complete the local map across final organic at this phi0. This checks whether the optimum plateau extends upward in phi1 or whether the critical pair deteriorates before the early-pair compression seen at even higher phi0.

For the final shot, fill the last untested interior neighbor between proven optima at (0.15,0.80), (0.20,0.80), and the 0.85 ridge. This completes the local map of the optimum plateau and checks whether a slightly lower phi1 at phi0 = 0.15 can still hold full resolution with minimal time cost.
